title: Rough seas, coastal surges impact several beachfront establishments
byline: Severe wave action and coastal surges have reportedly affected several beachfront establishments as rough sea conditions continue along parts of Sri Lanka’s coastline.

title: GMOA calls for immediate revision of health sector cadre
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) has called for an immediate revision of the approved cadre of doctors and other health workers, warning that delays could threaten the future stability of Sri Lanka’s free health service.

title: Man arrested over alleged LTTE camp hoax
byline: A 46-year-old man has been arrested by the Terrorism Investigation Division (TID) for allegedly spreading false and unverified information claiming that an LTTE training camp was operating inside a forest reserve in Akkarayankulam.

title: 19-year-old arrested over Rs. 10.4 mn ‘Undiyal’ transaction
byline: A 19-year-old man has been arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) under the provisions of the Money Laundering Act following the seizure of more than Rs. 10.4 million in cash during a raid in the Dam Street Police Division.

title: ‘This is the time’ to enter  Sri Lanka: CB Governor tells investors
byline: Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe yesterday urged the foreign investors to take a fresh look at Sri Lanka, arguing that the economy has moved beyond its crisis-era instability.

title: Sri Lanka on track to complete IMF programme by 2H27
byline: Sri Lanka is on course to complete its four-year programme with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in the second half of 2027, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe said, signalling confidence that the country can stay on track with the reform programme despite the heightened global uncertainty.

title: Elderly giraffe dies at Dehiwala Zoo
byline: An elderly female giraffe at the Dehiwala National Zoological Gardens died last night, the Department of National Zoological Gardens said.

title: Crosstalk in Parliament over proposed meeting of MPs, BASL tomorrow
byline: A crosstalk arose in Parliament today on the proposed meeting of a delegation from the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) and Members of Parliament with Leader of the House Bimal Ratnayake saying there is a procedural error with regard to the meeting tomorrow.

title: Child among nine foreign nationals killed in Indian city as fire burns down hotel
byline: A fire tore through a hotel in India’s eastern city of Kolkata, killing at least nine people including a child, the latest in a series of fire incidents in the state.

title: ‘Guardians’ programme promotes responsible care for street animals
byline: The “Guardians” programme, launched to encourage the public to care for street animals while taking responsibility for their health and welfare, is being introduced as a community-based approach to managing the country’s stray animal population.

title: Landmark trial on Meta’s impact on children’s mental health begins in US
byline: Opening statements in a landmark case against Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, have begun in the United States, with California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey accusing the social media giant of deliberately making its platforms addictive to young people.

title: No threat of another bankruptcy, Deputy Minister responds to Ranil
byline: Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe has rejected former President Ranil Wickremesinghe’s warning that Sri Lanka could face another economic crisis after 2028, saying there is no reason for the country to become bankrupt again.

title: All controversial matters in PTA amended in new Bill: Nalinda
byline: The Government has amended all the controversial matters existing in the Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act such as the definition of the word ’’terrorism’’ when the new Bill “Protection of the State from Terrorism Act” was drafted, Cabinet Spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said yesterday.

title: BASL to brief MPs on failure to fill judges’ vacancies in SC and AC
byline: A delegation of Bar Association Members will brief MPs on the failure to fill the existing judges’ vacancies in the Supreme Court and the Appeal Court, Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa told Parliament today.

title: Husband and mother-in-law charged over Indian bride’s death
byline: India’s federal police have filed charges in the case of a 33-year-old model and actor who was found dead in her matrimonial home in May just five months after her wedding.

title: Sri Lankan refugees in India allowed to return: Minister
byline: The Cabinet has decided to allow Sri Lankan  refugees to be domiciled in India to return to the island without any obstacles, Minister of Public Security Ananda Wijepala told Parliament today.

title: Seat belt law to be strictly enforced on expressways from September 19
byline: Police have warned that all passengers travelling in vehicles on Sri Lanka’s expressways will be required to wear seat belts from September 19, with the law to be strictly enforced.

title: 22 illegal structures demolished along Ahangama beach strip
byline: Authorities demolished at least 22 unauthorized structures, including several beachside restaurants and cafés, along the Ahangama beach strip yesterday.

title: Passenger drones could cost US$20–30 per trip from BIA to Colombo
byline: Tourists arriving at Bandaranaike International Airport could potentially travel to hotels in Colombo by passenger drone for an estimated fare of US$20–30 per trip under a proposed service being explored by Sri Lanka.

title: El Niño, Middle East crisis set to push food prices higher
byline: In the wake of the El Niño weather phenomenon affecting global agriculture and the Middle East crisis creating hurdles for shipping and trade, prices of imported food items, including essential commodities, are likely to rise by 20-25 percent in the coming months, importers warn.

title: SL envoy seeks stronger India partnership while safeguarding sovereignty
byline: Sri Lanka’s High Commissioner to India Mahishini Colonne has stressed the need to protect Sri Lanka’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and strategic autonomy while further strengthening its strategic partnership with India.

title: NMSJ warns 22A could place SC in conflict of interest
byline: The National Movement for Social Justice (NMSJ) has urged lawmakers to reconsider the proposed extension of the terms of Supreme Court and Court of Appeal judges, warning that the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution could place the Supreme Court in a position where it may have to hear a case concerning the tenure of its own judges.

title: Digital signature, paperless customs system to come into operation from October 1
byline: The Head of the Revenue Administration Reform and Modernization Bureau and Senior Additional Secretary to the President, Seevali Arukgoda, commended the contribution of the Information Technology Division of Sri Lanka Customs towards the successful implementation of the Digital Signature and Paperless Customs Declaration System, which is scheduled to come into operation from October 1.

title: Tamil Nadu announces one-year maternity leave for third child
byline: The Tamil Nadu government on Tuesday announced that woman government employees will be entitled to 365 days of maternity leave for their third child, from the current 12 weeks. Human Resources Management Minister D Sarathkumar announced this in the Assembly during the demand for grants discussion.

title: Sacked Ukrainian defence minister calls for presidential election
byline: Ukraine’s popular ex-defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov has called for wartime elections, in what is widely seen as the biggest challenge to Volodymyr Zelensky’s presidency since Russia’s full-scale invasion four and a half years ago.

title: Former Minister Jagath Pushpakumara’s wife passes away
byline: The wife of former Cabinet Minister and Monaragala District MP Jagath Pushpakumara has passed away following an accident.

title: Suthar six-fer seals India’s 165-run win in Galle
byline: India sealed a 165-run victory over Sri Lanka in the first Test at Galle, taking a 1-0 lead in the two-match series despite a brave fight from Sonal Dinusha.

title: UNFPA, NYSC train 100 young leaders in disaster preparedness
byline: The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), in partnership with the National Youth Services Council (NYSC) and under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, recently conducted a national simulation-based programme to strengthen youth participation in disaster preparedness and response.

title: Taking money to sign bail costs two years in jail
byline: Two men from Sanchi Arachchiwatta, Colombo, who were found guilty of accepting money to sign bail for an Indian national and submitting forged documents to court, were sentenced to two years’ rigorous imprisonment by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama today.

title: Demolition of Ahangama beachfront businesses makes no sense: SJB
byline: SJB National Youth Organizer Chamith Wijesundera has criticised the demolition of beachfront businesses in Ahangama, saying the move makes little sense while Sri Lanka’s economy remains fragile.

title: BASL president addresses high court of Bhutan during historic visit
byline: Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) President Rajeev Amarasuriya addressed the High Court of Bhutan during the first-ever visit by a BASL delegation to the Kingdom of Bhutan, as the two countries’ legal professions sought to strengthen cooperation and exchange experiences in the administration of justice.

title: CSE extends decline as ASPI slips below 21,450 despite foreign buying
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange extended its negative momentum for a second consecutive session on Wednesday, 19 August 2026, with both benchmark indices closing lower amid continued selling pressure across the broader market.

title: Honorary Consul hits back at Foreign Ministry over Guinea proposal
byline: Sri Lanka’s Honorary Consul in Guinea, Dr. Anuruddha Shanaka, has hit back at the Foreign Ministry’s response to his proposal to promote tourism and broader economic cooperation with the West African country, arguing that the Ministry’s reliance on the lack of direct air connectivity and tourist arrivals was “fundamentally misplaced” and irrelevant to the strategic merits of the initiative.
